messages:
sasha: heads-up, seeing a small set (~20) of users flip in and out of our RBAC groups over the last 3 hours. looks like deprovision -> re-provision loop. noticed session claim changes in SAML assertions around the same time. anyone else?

andrew: can you paste an example assertion? is this only for one idp / tenant?

sasha: here's a redacted example from logs (i replaced values). the changing claim is `entitlements` -> sometimes present, sometimes empty string:

```
<saml:Assertion ...>
  <saml:AttributeStatement>
    <saml:Attribute Name="email">
      <saml:AttributeValue>user@example.com</saml:AttributeValue>
    </saml:Attribute>
    <saml:Attribute Name="eduPersonEntitlement">
      <saml:AttributeValue>app:team:writer</saml:AttributeValue>
    </saml:Attribute>
  </saml:AttributeStatement>
</saml:Assertion>
```

sasha: then later assertion for same user is missing `eduPersonEntitlement` and SCIM deprovs happen.

rebecca: is the IdP sending different assertions for different sessions? might be idp-side session refresh dropping group claims. which idp is this? okta?

maria: it's an Okta tenant (corp-okta). i've seen Okta send minimal assertions on refresh if group filtering is enabled. we added a filter last week for that tenant.

andrew: that matches. SCIM deprov is triggered when the provisioning service receives change events -> deprovision user role if entitlement claim absent. our flow currently trusts assertion->entitlement for session-based RBAC sync.

rebecca: for mitigation can we stop immediate deprov on missing claim and instead use audit window (e.g., 24h grace) + fallback to last-known groups in DB?

sasha: yes please. current setting is `scim.deprov_immediate=true`. recommend flipping to `false` for that tenant while we triage.

provisioner-bot: action queued: set `scim.deprov_immediate=false` for tenant corp-okta. requested by sasha. ETA 2m. :white_check_mark:

maria: also seeing KMS decrypts for provisioning event payloads occasionally failing with transient errors around the same timeframe. not sure if related but adding here. log snippet: `kms:Decrypt failed: context mismatch`

andrew: hmm KMS failures could cause event retries/race and duplicate reconcile runs which might amplify churn. which KMS key? customer-managed or platform?

maria: platform KMS alias `projects/redwood/kms/keys/provisioner` (not customer-managed).

rebecca: for short-term triage: 1) flip deprov_immediate=false (done) 2) enable verbose tracing on provisioner for that tenant (dump event id + assertion id) 3) ask IdP team to confirm group-filter changes and session refresh behavior 4) add a temporary dedupe: if same user was deprov'd and reprovisioned within 5m, suppress alerts.

andrew: i'll add a tracing flag and create a lightweight roll-forward. trace id pattern: `prov-<tenant>-<epoch>` in logs. please include correlation_id from assertion if available.

sasha: i kicked off a support ticket with Okta (INC-72342). linking their response when they confirm filter behavior.

idp-probe-bot: IdP probe scheduled for corp-okta: session-assertion-sample x100, sampling rate 1%. results will post to #eng-security/incidents when ready.

maria: one more ask — can we add an audit log entry for when we flip deprov policy per tenant? want a clear trail for security/compliance.

rebecca: yes — adding `scim.policy.change` event to the audit stream, include user, admin, old_value, new_value, reason.

andrew: follow-ups: i'll check KMS decrypt error histogram and link to repro events; rebecca, please add the audit event; sasha please paste any Okta ticket updates. good catch. :thumbsup:

sasha: thanks all, will post updates here.
